answer: Each identity claims one canyon transect, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a timber estimate. The estimate is anchored at the transect nadir, its lowest point, and computed from the public canyon table as area times timber density. The auditor recomputes it; a mismatch or reuse burns the bond. The first fee is 35; the kth fee is 35+4(k-1), so the 1000th is 4031 and 1000 fakes pay 2,033,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-cruise ring fails because a borrowed cruise carries another transect and nadir, so recomputation mismatches. An honest filer pays 35 and redeems the bond after a clean epoch.
